question: to the Commission Manon Aubry (The Left), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), Emma Fourreau (The Left), Rima Hassan (The Left), Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Mélissa Camara (Verts/ALE), Arash Saeidi (The Left), David Cormand (Verts/ALE), Damien Carême (The Left), Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Leila Chaibi (The Left) Subject:

On 16 April 2024, the Commission received a complaint from the law firm Huglo Lepage alleging an infringement by the French State and asking for the matter to be referred to the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU). This complaint alleges that France is systematically breaching several European directives by granting environmental permits for major projects that are incompatible with its obligations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, without offsetting these emissions. The A69 motorway project, in particular, has been granted an environmental permit, and the complainants contest the procedure for assessing its impact on the climate. They also raise the issue of the Commission’s failure to respond to this complaint. In the meantime, the French Government has authorised several road projects, thus concreting over vast tracts of land and undermining efforts to combat climate change. Work on the A69 is not yet complete: a clear response from the Commission would send a strong message that the public has long been waiting for. Can the Commission therefore: 1.
provide a status update on the processing of this complaint and acknowledge receipt of it?
refer the matter to the CJEU?
take all necessary steps to compel Member States, and in particular France, to comply with the aforementioned legislation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.7.2026) The complaint mentioned by the Honourable Members concerns France’s alleged breach of the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive1 through the failure of the French authorities and courts to take full account of the impacts of road projects on climate change. As regards the A69 motorway project, which is mentioned as an example in the complaint and which is referred to by the Honourable Members, the Commission recalls that it has been subject to several court cases and administrative proceedings in France and that the main court case is now pending before the Council of State (Conseil d’Etat), the French supreme administrative court. The complaint is being examined by the Commission services. The complainant has already received an acknowledgement of receipt and will be informed of the next steps. In its role as guardian of the Treaties, the Commission monitors the application of EU law and may decide to take appropriate action, in line with its enforcement priorities2.
1 Directive 2011/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on the assessment

of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment, OJ L 26, 28.1.2012, p. 1-21. 2 Communication from the Commission - EU law: Better results through better application, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p. 10–20, and Communication from the Commission - Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers, 13.10.2022, COM(2022) 518 final.
